component.name: BT Handsfree
component.summary: Control phone calls over Bluetooth from the tray

description.p: BT Handsfree turns your Linux desktop into a Bluetooth hands-free unit for a phone connected over Bluetooth. Incoming calls show up as notifications with Answer and Reject buttons, and the tray menu lets you hang up, dial a number, call a contact, send DTMF tones, adjust call volume and choose whether call audio plays on the computer or stays on the phone. Contacts are read from the phone over Bluetooth and also name the callers of incoming calls; text messages arrive as notifications and can be read in conversations. The phone's battery level is shown alongside its name.
The app relies on PipeWire's native Bluetooth hands-free support and its telephony D-Bus service, so it needs PipeWire 1.4 or newer configured with the native HFP backend.

Developed and tested with one Android phone. iPhones use the same Bluetooth profiles and should work for calls, but have not been tried; contacts and messages depend on iOS permissions and expose less.

screenshot.caption: The dialpad with a number ready to call

description.p: Settings window with three tabs: the phones connected now and the other phones paired with the computer, the call audio controls and the About page. Choose which of the computer's speakers and microphones carry calls. Contacts stored with a national trunk zero now match the international number the phone reports, so calls and conversations show the contact's name.
Fix the tray icon and the notification icon being missing when the desktop cannot resolve the Flatpak's icon name: both now carry the icon's pixels.
First release published as a single-file Flatpak bundle on the GitHub releases page. No functional changes.

First release: incoming-call notifications, answer, reject, hang up, dial, contacts with caller ID, text messages with notifications, DTMF tones, call volume, audio routing and phone battery in the tray.
